issues.on_page: Sched 29 Disbursements: Electric 771,288; Sched 28 (p35): Electric accrual disbursements 85,425 (all depreciation, removed) + Inc (Dec) Prepaids/Due To 771,288 = cash basis 771,288
issues.issue: All of the Electric cash-basis 'disbursement' is an interfund due-to payment to other funds (an interfund loan or advance), not utility spending. It is recorded as a utilities expenditure. Sched 28 prints this breakdown, so it should go to other financing (or be left out), not expenditure.

issues.on_page: Sched 29 Receipts: Water 890,116; Sched 28 (p35): accrual 389,842 + receivables 4,342 + Due Froms 495,932
issues.issue: 495,932 of this water-charges revenue is interfund due-from money received from other funds, not water revenue. It is counted as revenue. Sched 28 prints the split: 394,184 is receipts and 495,932 is interfund, which belongs in other financing (split_from).

issues.on_page: Contributions/grants 665,809 (incl. Grant Project grant income 434,445 p33, Parks contributions/grants 189,441 p20)
issues.issue: Exhibit B (p2) shows these as operating grants (448,490 economic development) and capital grants (185,965 culture and recreation). If the grantor is a government (e.g. CDBG, state grants), most of this belongs in intergovernmental/state aid or federal grants, not private donations. The grantor isn't stated.

Debt principal and interest payments in fund schedules are recorded as 'other financing'. At the top level the same payments are disbursements (outside_printed_total). Because of this, detail never shows them as debt principal / debt interest and fees spending. Same for detail[42], [93], [94], [141], [142], [166], [167].
